column2: The new drill is a hard one: pikes and halberds in close order, handgunners firing by ranks, a charge of horse to test the line. You ride the front yourself to show the men how it is done. A horse shies, a pike swings wide, and the next thing you know you are on your back in the mud with the surgeon kneeling over you.
The wound will heal. The drill goes on.
I will carry this mark for the rest of my days.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation. It is a clean wound and the surgeon says I will mend. The drill goes on without me until I can sit a horse again.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

My liege,

A word from the drill yard: I was hurt while putting the men through a new formation, and the surgeon could not save all of me. I am still your marshal and I will still serve, though I will never again lead a charge the way I did.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Such is the price of a strong army.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] keeps the finest soldiers in the province, and everyone knows why. [From.GetSheHeCap] has drill books of [From.GetHerHis] own, copied from veterans of a dozen campaigns: how to hold a square against cavalry, how to march a column through a forest without losing half of it. If [From.GetSheHe] could be talked into sharing them...
I will ask [From.GetHerHim] myself.
The lord will be asked to share the drill books.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], marshal of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has called on you with wine and compliments. What [From.GetSheHe] really wants are your drill books, which have cost you years of campaigning to put together.
Take them, and use them well.
Some secrets stay in the family.
The marshal will learn the lord's secrets.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent over [From.GetHerHis] drill books, bound in old leather and full of notes in the margins. Half of it you knew already. The other half will change the way the army fights.
My liege must hear of this generosity.
Your liege will gain the secrets.

My liege,

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has shared [FromFrom.GetHerHis] drill books with me, and I have already begun teaching their lessons to the men. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] deserves your thanks.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
A loyal subject indeed.

The drills of the past months have paid off. Word has spread that the liege's marshal feeds the men well and pays on time, and fresh levies keep turning up at the muster: farmers' sons, discharged mercenaries and a few men nobody asks too many questions about.
More spears for the realm.
The province will refill its levies faster.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] reports that the drill has drawn fresh men to the muster in [From.Location.GetName]. The levies there will be quick to fill again.
Good work, Marshal.

You have come to drill the levies of [From.Location.GetName], but one of the lords there keeps finding reasons why [From.GetHerHis] men cannot come: the harvest, a fever, a broken bridge. Nobody believes a word of it. [From.GetSheHeCap] simply does not want [From.GetHerHis] men learning to march to the liege's drum.
Send [From.GetHerHim] a sharp letter.
The lord will answer.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] writes, in the name of your liege, that your levies are to report for drill without further delay. The tone is not friendly.
My men stay on my land.
Very well. Let them march.
The marshal will write to the liege.

My liege,

[From.GetTitledFirstName] refuses to send [From.GetHerHis] levies to the drill. I have done what I can, but [From.GetSheHe] answers my letters with excuses and insults. The men of [FromFrom.Location.GetName] will be slow to answer your call to arms until this is settled.

Your servant,
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]
[From.GetSheHeCap] will regret this.

Word went round the longhouses that the liege wants fighting men, and they came: young warriors who have never taken a head, old ones who have run out of plunder, outlaws who want their names back. They are eager, they are hungry and they are already asking where the raiding is.
Follow me to our chief!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has brought a war band to your hall, raised from every corner of the land. They will follow you wherever there is loot, but they will not sit idle for long.
Then let us find them something to burn.

The raiders [From.GetTitledFirstName] raised for you have sat by your fires for months, eating your food and waiting for the raid you promised. Now they have had enough. Before they go home they want what they are owed, and they make it clear that they will take it one way or another.
Pay them and be rid of them.

Harvest was good in [Root.Location.GetName], and you made sure the liege's share was counted twice and collected once, with a little extra for the roads, the bridges and the walls that nobody will ever see built. The peasants grumbled, but they paid. A heavy chest is ready to go home.
Send it to the treasury.
Your liege will receive the tithe.
A chest arrives from [From.GetTitledFirstName], sealed with your steward's mark: a tithe from [From.Location.GetName], squeezed out of the peasants with the usual care.
Into the treasury it goes.

The tax rolls have been read out in the square once too often. This time the crowd does not scatter. Someone throws a stone, someone else a pitchfork, and the whole village surges towards you, shouting that they will hang the steward from the church bell.
Run!
You may get away.
You may be wounded.
You make it to your horse with the mob at your heels and do not stop until you see the walls of the castle. Your dignity is somewhere back in the mud, along with your hat.
That was too close.
The mob catches up with you at the edge of the village. By the time the guards beat them back you have been dragged through the mud and given a beating you will feel for months.
Ungrateful wretches!
Your liege will be told.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was attacked by peasants while collecting taxes in [From.Location.GetName], and badly hurt.
Noted.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was dragged off [From.GetHerHis] horse by peasants while collecting taxes in [From.Location.GetName], and beaten to death in the street.
Find me a new steward.

You have squeezed [Root.Location.GetName] hard this year, and it shows. Granaries stand empty, the taverns are full of angry talk, and the bailiffs say men are meeting in the woods at night. The liege's taxes will be paid, but not gladly.
The liege must be told.

Word comes from [From.Location.GetName]: [From.GetTitledFirstName], the steward of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], has taxed the province so hard that the peasants are close to rising. Your own lands there may not stay quiet.
Trouble is coming.

My liege,

The people of [From.Location.GetName] are close to revolt over the taxes. The money is coming in, but the lords of the province blame you for it, and so do the peasants.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
They will pay all the same.

Among the masons on the walls of [Root.Location.GetName] you have found a true master: a grey old builder who learned his trade on the walls of a great city and can tell a bad stone just by tapping it. With him at your side, every work you oversee will go faster.
Hire him for life.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

I have taken a master builder into service. The works in [From.Location.GetName] are already going faster, and the people are glad of the work.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Well found.

Something is wrong with the works in [Root.Location.GetName]. Scaffolding collapses overnight, mortar will not set, and carts of good stone go missing on the road. The masons whisper that one of the local lords does not want the liege building here.
I will find out who.
The lord will decide what to do.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], the steward of [From.Liege.GetTitledFirstName], is building in [From.Location.GetName], right under your nose. If the work goes well, your liege will be stronger here, and you will be weaker. A few bribed masons could change that.
Pay the masons to botch it.
Leave the works alone.
The works will be sabotaged.
A whole section of the new wall has come down in the night, and half the masons have run off with their wages. Someone paid for this.
Write to the liege.
Your liege will hear of it.

My liege,

The works in [From.Location.GetName] have been sabotaged. It will take a year to make good what was lost.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Start again.

Your agents have followed the money behind the sabotage in [FromFrom.Location.GetName]. The bribed masons all drink in the same tavern, and the man who paid them wears the colours of [From.GetTitledFirstName].
The liege must know.
Your liege will learn who it was.

My liege,

The sabotage of your works was paid for by [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]. I have the masons' confessions if you need them.

Your servant,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will remember this.
Let it go.
The people of [Root.Location.GetName] have given up the old ways. They speak our tongue, keep our feasts and send their sons to our wars. The land is ours now, and not only on the map.
It is done.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] reports that the people of [From.Location.GetName] have taken up our ways.
Our land now.
Not everyone in [Root.Location.GetName] wants to be settled. A band of locals ambushes you on the road, and you get away with a blade in your side.
I will live.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] was ambushed and wounded by locals while settling [From.Location.GetName]. [From.GetSheHeCap] has not given up.
A brave servant.

You have spent months telling the deeds of [Root.Liege.GetTitledFirstName] in every hall and camp of the land, and the tales have spread. Now young warriors come every day, wanting to fight for a lord whose name is in the songs.
Bring them to the liege.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] arrives at the head of a crowd of warriors, all of them drawn by tales of your deeds. They want to fight for you, and they want to do it soon.
Welcome, warriors!
The warriors drawn by your fame have waited a year for a war that never came. One by one they have packed up and gone home, telling everyone they meet that your legend is all talk.
Let them go.

[event_target:tribute_giver.GetTitledFirstName] keeps a rich camp in [Root.Location.GetName], and [event_target:tribute_giver.GetSheHe] could easily spare more for [event_target:tribute_asker.GetTitledFirstName]. Of course, [event_target:tribute_giver.GetSheHe] may not see it that way.
Demand more.
I dare not.
The lord will be asked for a year's income.

[From.GetTitledFirstName], steward of [event_target:tribute_asker.GetTitledFirstName], has come to your camp. [From.GetSheHeCap] wants a year's income on top of what you already pay, and makes it clear that this is not a request.
Pay.
Refuse.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has paid the extra tribute, with very bad grace.
Excellent.
Your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName] has squeezed a year's income out of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName].
Excellent.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has refused to pay any more tribute and had you thrown out of the camp.
The liege will hear of this.
[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has refused your steward [From.GetTitledFirstName]'s demand for extra tribute.
Insolence!
